title: Evaluating the Evaluators: Investigating LLM Judges for Personalized Writing Style Assessment
gist: Apple researchers test how well LLM judges assess personalized writing style versus human labels, finding judge quality only weakly correlated with MMLU ability (Pearson's ρ ≤ 0.2), better with pairwise comparison than independent scoring, and that the 'strongest' LLMs are not the most reliable proxies for human judgment.

themes.theme: Judge quality decoupled from model capability

insights.claim: In Apple's study of LLM judges for personalized writing tasks, judge quality correlates only weakly with general LLM ability as measured by MMLU (Pearson's ρ ≤ 0.2).
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Benchmark leaderboards are poor guides for picking an evaluator model; evaluation stacks need task-specific validation.

insights.claim: The 'strongest' LLMs do not most reliably reproduce human evaluations of personalized writing, which Apple researchers hypothesize stems from exaggerated sensitivity to subtle details that human annotators and weaker LLMs ignore.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Paying for frontier models as judges may buy worse human alignment, favoring cheaper evaluators and custom eval tooling.
